steps.title: Create one seed box
steps.body: Build one small box that will act as the repeated element for both rotational workflows.

success.prompt: A compact box exists and is ready for array operations.

steps.title: Think about the center first
steps.body: Before launching an array tool, decide where the center, reference arm, and sweep direction should live. These tools depend on pick order.

actions.description: Use an overview camera while planning the center.

success.prompt: You know where the rotation center and sweep should be.

steps.title: Build a rotational array
steps.body: Activate Rotational Array and place copies around a shared center point to form an arc or ring.

success.prompt: The seed box has been copied around a center.

steps.title: Check increment and sweep
steps.body: Look for whether the angular increment and the final sweep point agree. If the result is empty or odd, redo the picks with a clearer span.
steps.notes: This mirrors the runtime messages used by the tool when increment or sweep become invalid.

success.prompt: The rotational copies read as an intentional arc or circle.

steps.title: Switch to a helical array
steps.body: Activate Helical Array and define the rising sweep so each copy advances in angle and height.
steps.notes: This is the right tool when the pattern should climb like a spiral stair, thread, or tower study.

success.prompt: The copies rise while rotating around the center.
